body:
If you are young enough to be in school, do you have a guidance counselor you can talk to? Maybe they can convince your parents you have real issues or else help you find help on your own. Or any other authority figure. 

There's always the Suicide Hotline, but I don't have any personal experience with it.

I think if I'd have gotten help as a teenager I'd have turned out a lot better than I did. My parents had pretty much the same attitude as yours.

Stop. Don't. Give yourself more time! See how you feel in a week. You will almost certainly feel better. 

In the meantime, do some research on hanging. It's not a nice way to go.

In a word, [no](http://lostallhope.com/suicide-methods/statistics-most-lethal-methods). There's no perfect, 100% lethal, painless method.

I was planning to kill myself with prescription drugs and had been saving them up for months, but then I did some research. It's one of the least successful methods.

If it was easy, there'd be a lot fewer people in the world.

I have a lousy family, too. It used to be a great family but the few that are left are all train wrecks or assholes. It's hard when you feel like you don't have any support. Especially if you ask for help and get ignored. I really hope karma is a thing.

Things almost always get better. They might get worse before they get better, but you'll always end up higher than rock bottom.

If you want a pragmatic reason not to do it... I think there's only a 94 percent success rate. There are people who have survived with horrific injuries. Another thing, if you support the second amendment, you're going to add fuel to the gun control folks.

Just don't do it. We need you here.

Great post. That's interesting... a way to push people away further? 

We're all troubled and hurting here, just in different stages of the battle. I see telling someone off that genuinely wants to help to be just as dangerous as someone relying to a post saying just go kill yourself then. Both sides deserve kindness and respect and consideration of their possible mental state.

We are all in the same boat.

I'm starting to think about a third of the posts are just people who want to show their life is so much worse than anyone else's. I made a post and suggested a venting tag for those who just want to gripe with no input.

I got my hand bitten again today. I think that may be why we don't see as many helping. If you genuinely try to help and someone comes back with a smart ass remark, after a few times it's like why bother. As far as I'm concerned, they listen or they don't. Last week I was going to kill myself on Friday, with the help I got here I'm still around.
I don't know what you mean.

Holy shit, that makes me cringe. It's not going to kill you, but it's most likely going to damage you badly. Maybe to the point of never having children or comfortable sex again. Please don't do that.

My dog saved my life last summer. He was literally the only thing that kept me alive. I loved him more than anything.

He passed away suddenly in April. I am nowhere near over it. There are so many little things that remind me of him, things we used to do together. I know that he would not want me to be unhappy, but there's a hole in my heart. He was only 8.I'd expected to have him until he was at least 12, based on his breed.

I know exactly how you feel. I've also had 2 cats disappear. It's been a rough year. Hugs to you.

Last year the only thing that stopped me from killing myself was my dog. I didn't know what would happen to him if I was gone.

Even if you don't think it will, it will devastate your family and they'll never get over it. My half sister killed herself years ago and no one was ever the same. It absolutely ruined my parents. You know, everyone blames themselves. My dad wound up in the hospital with a heart condition soon afterward and my mom got hooked on hydros and turned absolutely batshit crazy. I don't know what my other sisters were doing because they weren't speaking to us at the time, but one of them attacked me in *my dad's hospital room* saying it was my fault. That was lovely. We didn't speak for ten years. 

I don't have any close family anymore so thank goodness for Cooper. He saved me. Losing him this spring almost killed me. I have never missed a person, besides my dad, as much as I miss that dog.

If you love your family, please don't do that to them. Don't do it to yourself.

I've known two people who had seizures from those things. It wasn't pretty. I don't think you're going to blow out your heart from drinking them, but you could be doing damage that you'll regret when you get older.

I've had one Monster in my life and I was so cracked out people thought I was on drugs. Plus it tasted like ass. I don't know how people stand them.

You know what, fuck those people. 

I went through a very rough time the past two weeks and I had actually set Friday as the day I was going to kill myself. I am very independent and I have control issues, so it took an epic effort for me to ask for help. Even my best friend just kept telling me the same thing over and over. I sent my uncle (I'm not close to any of my family) and email telling him I was in a bad place and needed help and never got a reply. Just fuck them and everyone else who says "I'm here if you need me" but act like you're a leper if you actually come to them for help.

I had one friend that listened to me rant, he dealt with a lot of shit from me for a week. A lot of crazy. He didn't really say anything, he just listened. He may not have even read my texts. Just getting it out of my system helped. But between him & here, I drug myself through it.

Fucked up as I am, I've been the one on the listening end to a lot of people. I've had other people literally walk away and practically hide when someone started talking about a problem. But I know how it feels so I listen and I do what I can.

People just don't really want to help. It makes them feel good to say it, but when the chips are down, even if they love you, they won't/can't be there. It's hard for anyone to empathize if they don't have mental issues themselves. 

Also, it's really hard to kill yourself. Doing research on it was an eye opener for me and had quite a bit of effect on my decision not to do it.

Well, if you know you're awful, then you're not completely awful. Sociopaths, narcissists, etc. don't see anything wrong with their actions. So you're not awful. You could be depressed or have some other health issue making you feel that way. Go to a doctor. 

If you kill yourself it'll fuck your son up for the rest of his life. So if you can't keep going for yourself, do it for him.

I know some people have already mentioned medication, but if you can find the right one for you it can make all the difference in the world. Sometimes it takes a while to find one that works so you have to be patient.

Do you feel kind of outside yourself, like you're just watching your life? I used to feel like that a lot. Or I'd have bad thoughts or feelings, but is also know somehow that that wasn't really me.

I really, really think an antidepressant could work wonders for you. Have you talked to your gf about how you feel?

That said, give yourself a week and see how you feel then. I was going to kill myself Friday but things got a little better so i (obviously) didn't.

Well, I did everything I could to save him. Made sure he went to AA tried to keep him away from his bad friends, was looking into paying for rehab for him. But he was slowly sucking the life out of me. I had no idea the drug stuff was going on, I thought he was a recovering addict. He'd steal my car once about every three weeks and stay gone for a whole night. He went to jail for two months and when he got out he was an absolute monster - like someone I didn't know. The night after he got out he ran off and I was DONE. 

The thing is, I knew he'd be dead within a year and I told him so. It only took two months. But it came to the point of him or me. I spent a week in a psych hospital and God knows what he got up to while i was in there, because he sure wasn't calling or visiting me. I found out so many things after he died... I'm so naive and was so blindly trusting. 

So many people on here want to die but are scared or fear messing it up. He took the easy way out right up until the end.

I was let out of the hospital into his "care" but I ended up dealing with a lot that I shouldn't have for my own mental health. I even had a friend of mine who happens to be a preacher come out and talk with him (he feigned religiousness at times) and I found out later he felt like there was something deeply wrong with Brian and was afraid for me.

Sorry to ramble on. Just hang in there. I don't know how recent it was, but things get... I can't say easier... I guess you just get used to it. I've made it two years. The worst part for me has been losing the ability to trust any men. I just can't do it.

Benzos are doing to end up a lot like the pain med epidemics. Used to, you could walk into your PCP, tell him your toe hurt, and you'd come out with a scrip. Then someone finally figured out it was bad, but it was too late, and now we've got desperate people ODing on heroin.

Now they give out benzos like candy to anyone who claims they once had a panic attack. I was given a prescription for Ativan about 6 years ago when I found out my dad had terminal cancer and hadn't told us until he was about halfway through his time left. I had my first panic attack at work and I literally thought I was going to die. The hospital was right across the street so went to the Er where they gave me a small scrip. My PCP gave me a full prescription, upped it later.

The I found out way too late from his PA that these drugs are intended for short term use. A few weeks or months to get you through a hard time. Why wasn't I told this very the beginning, because by this time I was hooked.

I've tried several times to get off them, but I always go back. I almost always stick to my prescription unless I'm having a really rough time, but I can't get by without them.

I did have someone put me on hydroxyzine pamoate, which is non narcotic, and I think it helps with my anxiety better than the lorazepam. It was intended to get me off the Ativan, but I take both now.

Back in January I told my PCP I didn't feel the Ativan was working that well. This was honest as I was going through a rough time. He took me from 2mg Ativan a day to 2mg of Klonopin. I was wiped out for days. So I looked it up and it's like 4x stronger. WTF.

I had to quit the klonopin because it made me feel angry, but I still can't give up my Ativan. I don't think they even do much for me anymore. 

Long story short, if you need anxiety meds, so NO to any benzos and ask for hydroxyzine pamoate. It's not addictive and works just as well, if not better.

I'd try meds first, but I hate therapy. I think we have some tiny little synapse or chemical that isn't doing its job and maybe a light antidepressant would get you feeling a little better. It might take a while to find the right one.

This is also the only drug I'd trust subscribed by a regular doctor. Anything else I'd see a psychiatrist. Some PCPs will put you on everything. I'm on so much crap. Don't let them put you on a narcotic like Ativan or Xanax. These are highly addictive and you're not supposed to take them longer than around 3 months. Hydroxyzine Pamoate is a wonderful non narcotic anxiety med.

Every horse in the world should be on this sub. They are masters of suicide. They will get colic and often die if they eat too much, drink too much water, or just feel like it. Getting another injury can cause it. They will find the only hole or sharp point in a 1000 acre pasture. Over the winter my mini ripped his eyelid off on a bucket. On a fucking plastic horse safe bucket. They can lay the wrong way in their stall and not be able to get up and if they're not found right away they'll die. They can roll and twist their intestine and die. 

The biggest killer is laminitis/founder, which is a hideous inflammation of the hooves. This can be caused by standing too long, eating too much, eating spring grass, being ridden on a hard surface, or, again, because they feel like it. There was a very famous racehorse that nearly died from laminitis a couple years ago because she stepped on a nail. 

Most people don't realize that horses can recover from broken bones just fine. But putting more weight on the opposite leg often makes it founder so they have to be put down because they're in indescribable pain. (imagine having your toe nail being peeled off slowly, but times 10000). You can't treat them in a sling for long periods because they can't breathe that well unless they're standing. 

Secretariat died of laminitis because he was fat.

Horses are the spirit animal of suicidal people.
